note: The raw fuzzer input is written unchanged to a temporary .pcap file, so the candidate controls the packet bytes read by PcapPlusPlus.
The pcap packet captured length allocates exactly the heap buffer that backs the RawPacket data.
The crafted Ethernet/IPv4/GRE bytes are copied into the heap buffer with no extra trailing bytes.

code: m_NextLayer = IPv4Layer::isDataValid(payload, payloadLen) ? static_cast<Layer*>(new IPv4Layer(payload, payloadLen, this, m_Packet)) : static_cast<Layer*>(new PayloadLayer(payload, payloadLen, this, m_Packet));
note: EtherType 0x0800 makes the Ethernet layer parse the controlled payload as IPv4.
The IPv4 protocol byte 47 selects GRE parsing; the IPv4 payload is only the 4-byte GRE basic header.
The only GRE length gate requires the 4-byte basic header, which is true for the candidate, but GREv1 later requires an 8-byte gre1_header.
The parser constructs a GREv1Layer based only on the version bits and does not validate payloadLen >= sizeof(gre1_header).
The fuzz target invokes recalculation after parsing, causing the malformed GREv1 layer to update writable header fields.
Packet recalculation dispatches to the last parsed layer first, including the malformed GREv1 layer.
Writing the 16-bit GREv1 payloadLength field at offset 4 overflows the 4-byte GRE heap slice by two bytes.
